source.text: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ לְדָוִ֗ד מִזְמ֥וֹר שִֽׁיר׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director. Of David. A psalm. A song.

en.L: For the director: of David; a psalm; a song.
en.B: For the music director. Of David. A psalm. A song.
en.R: For the leader of the music. A song of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: a hard and ancient song
decisions.reason: Psalm 68 has more rare words than almost any other psalm, and many lines are hard to read with certainty. It seems to follow God's march from Sinai through the wilderness to his dwelling on Zion, and on to the homage of the nations. Its language is close to the old songs of Exodus 15, Deuteronomy 33 and Judges 5.

decisions.choice: A song of David
decisions.reason: Readable gives one plain word for the two words for a song.

source.text: יָק֣וּם אֱ֭לֹהִים יָפ֣וּצוּ אוֹיְבָ֑יו וְיָנ֥וּסוּ מְ֝שַׂנְאָ֗יו מִפָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Let God arise; let his enemies be scattered, and let those who hate him flee from before him.

en.L: Let God arise; let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies be scattered, and let those who hate {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} flee from before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Let God rise up and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies scatter; let all who hate {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} run from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.
en.R: Let God get up! Let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies run off in every direction. Let those who hate {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} run away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the song of the ark
decisions.reason: The line echoes the words Moses said whenever the ark set out: "Arise, LORD, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee before you" (Numbers 10:35). The psalm opens as a march of God at the head of his people. Here the verbs speak of God ("let God arise") and the text says "God" where Numbers has the name.

decisions.choice: let God arise: a wish or a statement
alternatives: God will arise, his enemies will be scattered
decisions.reason: The verbs can be read as wishes or as confident statements of what will happen. Verse 4 is clearly a wish, so the opening is read the same way.

decisions.choice: rise up (B); get up (R)
decisions.reason: As in the call "Arise, LORD" elsewhere in the Psalms (3:8; 7:7).

source.text: כְּהִנְדֹּ֥ף עָשָׁ֗ן תִּ֫נְדֹּ֥ף כְּהִמֵּ֣ס דּ֭וֹנַג מִפְּנֵי־אֵ֑שׁ יֹאבְד֥וּ רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים מִפְּנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: As smoke is driven, you drive [them]; as wax melts from before fire, let [the] wicked perish from before God.

en.L: As smoke is driven away, [so] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} drive [them] away; as wax melts before fire, let [the] wicked perish before God.
en.B: Blow them away as smoke is blown away; as wax melts in front of the flames, may the wicked come to nothing in God's presence.
en.R: Blow them away like smoke! Let evil people melt away before God like wax near a fire.

decisions.choice: you drive them: a word to God
decisions.reason: For a moment the psalm speaks to God directly ("you drive them away") before speaking of him again. The verb is the same as "driven": smoke driven by the wind.

decisions.choice: smoke and wax: what does not last
decisions.reason: Smoke scatters in the wind and wax runs in the heat (37:20; 97:5; Micah 1:4). God's enemies cannot stand before him.

decisions.choice: Blow them away
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the line a prayer to God, which is its force.

source.text: וְֽצַדִּיקִ֗ים יִשְׂמְח֣וּ יַֽ֭עַלְצוּ לִפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִ֗ים וְיָשִׂ֥ישׂוּ בְשִׂמְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] righteous, let them rejoice; let them exult before God and let them be glad with gladness.

en.L: But the righteous — let them rejoice; let them exult before God and be glad with gladness.
en.B: But let the righteous be glad and celebrate before God; let them be overjoyed.
en.R: But let people who do what is right be happy. Let them celebrate in front of God and be full of joy.

decisions.choice: but: the righteous set against the wicked
decisions.reason: The wicked perish before God (verse 3); the righteous rejoice before him.

decisions.choice: be glad with gladness: great joy
decisions.reason: A verb with its own noun stresses the action: they are full of joy.

decisions.choice: people who do what is right
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the Psalms, Readable says who the righteous are.

source.text: שִׁ֤ירוּ׀לֵֽאלֹהִים֮ זַמְּר֪וּ שְׁ֫מ֥וֹ סֹ֡לּוּ לָרֹכֵ֣ב בָּ֭עֲרָבוֹת בְּיָ֥הּ שְׁמ֗וֹ וְעִלְז֥וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Sing to God, sing praise [to] his name; build up [a way] for the one riding through the deserts — in Yah [is] his name — and exult before him.

en.L: Sing to God, sing praise [to] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; build up [a road] for the one who rides through the deserts — {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name — and exult before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Sing to God, make music to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; prepare a highway for the one who rides through the deserts. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name; celebrate before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!
en.R: Sing to God! Make music to honor {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name! Build a road for the one who rides across the desert. His name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}. Be happy in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!

decisions.choice: the deserts: the dry lands of the wilderness
alternatives: the clouds: lift up a song to the one who rides on the clouds
decisions.reason: The word ('aravot) usually means the dry plains or wilderness, and verse 8 has God marching through the wilderness. Many read it here as "clouds", because verse 34 has God "riding in the heavens" and an old title of a Canaanite storm god was "rider of the clouds"; the psalm would then claim that title for Israel's God.

decisions.choice: build up: raise a road
decisions.reason: The verb (salal) means to heap up earth for a road, as in Isaiah 62:10 and the call to prepare a highway in the desert (Isaiah 40:3). Some take it as "lift up" a song.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a shortened form of the name YHWH (as in Exodus 15:2 and in "Hallelu-yah"). It is rendered like the full name, with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: in Yah is his name: his name is Yah
decisions.reason: The small word "in" here marks what something is: his name is Yah.

source.text: אֲבִ֣י יְ֭תוֹמִים וְדַיַּ֣ן אַלְמָנ֑וֹת אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים בִּמְע֥וֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: A father of [the] fatherless and a judge of widows [is] God in [the] dwelling of his holiness.

en.L: A father of the fatherless and a judge of widows [is] God in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling.
en.B: From {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy dwelling God acts as father to orphans and defender of widows.
en.R: God lives in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy home. He is a father to children who have no father. He stands up for widows.

decisions.choice: judge: one who takes up their case
decisions.reason: A judge (dayyan) here is one who defends the rights of the weak in court. Widows and the fatherless had no one to speak for them (Deuteronomy 10:18).

decisions.choice: the holy God cares for the helpless
decisions.reason: The God who lives in holiness, far above, is the one who looks after those with no protector.

decisions.choice: God first in the sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God early for a clear sentence; the Hebrew holds the name back to the end.

source.text: אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀מ֘וֹשִׁ֤יב יְחִידִ֨ים׀בַּ֗יְתָה מוֹצִ֣יא אֲ֭סִירִים בַּכּוֹשָׁר֑וֹת אַ֥ךְ ס֝וֹרֲרִ֗ים שָׁכְנ֥וּ צְחִיחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: God [is] making [the] solitary dwell [in a] house; bringing out prisoners into prosperity; only [the] rebellious dwell [in] a scorched land.

en.L: God makes the solitary dwell in a home; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings out prisoners into prosperity; only the rebellious dwell [in] a scorched land.
en.B: God gives the lonely a home to live in; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads prisoners out into well-being, but rebels stay in a sunbaked land.
en.R: God gives lonely people a family and a home. He sets prisoners free and makes them prosper. But people who rebel against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} have to live in a dry, empty land.

decisions.choice: prosperity: a good and happy state
decisions.reason: The word (kosharot) is found only here. It seems related to a verb meaning "to succeed". Some connect it with a word for songs, "with singing".

decisions.choice: a house: a home, a family
decisions.reason: The word (bayit) means both a house and a household. People who are alone are given a place and a family to belong to.

decisions.choice: from slavery to the land
decisions.reason: The God who brought Israel out of Egypt ("brought out" is the Exodus verb) frees the captive; the rebels of the wilderness died in the desert (Numbers 14:29-35).

decisions.choice: against him
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they rebel against.

source.text: אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים בְּ֭צֵאתְךָ לִפְנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֑ךָ בְּצַעְדְּךָ֖ בִֽישִׁימ֣וֹן סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through [the] wasteland, Selah.

en.L: God, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} went out before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} marched through the wasteland, Selah
en.B: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} went out at the head of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} strode through the desert. Selah
en.R: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} went out in front of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. You marched with them through the desert. Selah

decisions.choice: the march through the wilderness
decisions.reason: Verses 8-9 are very close to the Song of Deborah: "LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the field of Edom, the earth shook, and the heavens dropped" (Judges 5:4-5). God led Israel from Egypt through the wilderness in the pillar of cloud and fire (Exodus 13:21).

decisions.choice: God in place of the name
decisions.reason: Judges 5:4 has the name, the LORD; this psalm says "God". Psalms 42-83 mostly say "God" ('elohim) where other psalms use the name. The word in the text is rendered.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The "when" clauses run on into verse 9, so Literal ends with a comma before the Selah. Balanced and Readable make this verse a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: you went out ... you strode
alternatives: when you went out ... when you marched
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the march as a fact, since Selah breaks the sentence.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: אֶ֤רֶץ רָעָ֨שָׁה׀אַף־שָׁמַ֣יִם נָטְפוּ֮ מִפְּנֵ֪י אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים זֶ֥ה סִינַ֑י מִפְּנֵ֥י אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: [the] earth quaked; even [the] heavens dropped before God, this Sinai, before God, [the] God of Israel.

en.L: the earth quaked; even the heavens dropped [rain] before God, the One of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
en.B: The earth trembled and the sky streamed with rain before God, the God of Sinai; before God, Israel's God.
en.R: The earth shook and rain poured down from the sky when God came, the God of Mount Sinai, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: this Sinai: the One of Sinai
decisions.reason: The words "this Sinai" are an old title, "the One of Sinai", as in Judges 5:5: the God who appeared on Mount Sinai. Some read "even Sinai itself (shook)".

decisions.choice: Sinai
decisions.reason: When God came down on Sinai the mountain shook and smoked (Exodus 19:16-18).

decisions.choice: dropped: poured down rain
decisions.reason: The verb (nataf) is to drip or pour; the next verse speaks of rain.

decisions.choice: rain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "dropped"; the next verse shows that rain is meant.

source.text: גֶּ֣שֶׁם נְ֭דָבוֹת תָּנִ֣יף אֱלֹהִ֑ים נַחֲלָתְךָ֥ וְ֝נִלְאָ֗ה אַתָּ֥ה כֽוֹנַנְתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Rain of free gifts you shed abroad, God; your inheritance, and it was weary, you made it firm.

en.L: A rain of free gifts {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} poured out, God; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, when it was weary, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made it firm.
en.B: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent showers of generous rain; when {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} land was worn out, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} restored it.
en.R: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent plenty of rain. Your land was dry and tired, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made it strong again.

decisions.choice: free gifts: generous, given freely
decisions.reason: The word (nedavot) is used for freewill offerings; here it is rain given freely and in plenty.

decisions.choice: your inheritance: your land, or your people
decisions.reason: God's inheritance (nachalah) is the land he gave Israel, and also Israel itself. The rain on a weary land fits the land best.

decisions.choice: your land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the inheritance is here (m2).

source.text: חַיָּתְךָ֥ יָֽשְׁבוּ־בָ֑הּ תָּ֤כִ֥ין בְּטוֹבָתְךָ֖ לֶעָנִ֣י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Your living [band], they dwelt in it; you prepared in your goodness for the poor, God.

en.L: Your band dwelt in it; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} provided in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodness for the poor, God.
en.B: Your flock found a home there; out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} goodness, God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made ready what the afflicted needed.
en.R: Your people came to live there. God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are good, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave poor people what they needed.

decisions.choice: your living band: your people, your flock
decisions.reason: The word (chayyah) usually means a living creature or animal; here it seems to mean a group or company (as in 2 Samuel 23:13), God's people pictured as his flock.

decisions.choice: the poor: the afflicted, humble people
decisions.reason: The word ('ani) means poor or afflicted. Here it is Israel itself, a weak people that God provided for in the land.

decisions.choice: in it: in the land
decisions.reason: "It" is the inheritance of verse 10, the land.

source.text: אֲדֹנָ֥י יִתֶּן־אֹ֑מֶר הַֽ֝מְבַשְּׂר֗וֹת צָבָ֥א רָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] Lord gives [the] word; the women who bear the news [are] a great host:

en.L: The Lord gives the word; the women who bring the news [are] a great host:
en.B: The Lord speaks the word, and a great army of women spreads the good news:
en.R: The Lord gives the command. Then a huge crowd of women spreads the good news:

decisions.choice: women who bring the news: women singing the victory
decisions.reason: The word for those who bring good news is feminine, as in Isaiah 40:9. In Israel women met the returning army with songs of victory (Exodus 15:20-21; Judges 5; 1 Samuel 18).

decisions.choice: the word: God's command, or the news of victory
decisions.reason: The word ('omer) is a spoken word. The Lord speaks, perhaps the command for battle or the word of victory, and the women spread it.

decisions.choice: what the women say
decisions.reason: The verse ends with a colon: the next verse gives the news they spread.

source.text: מַלְכֵ֣י צְ֭בָאוֹת יִדֹּד֣וּן יִדֹּד֑וּן וּנְוַת בַּ֝֗יִת תְּחַלֵּ֥ק שָׁלָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Kings of armies flee, they flee, and [the] beautiful one of [the] house divides plunder.

en.L: "Kings of armies flee, they flee, and she who stays at home divides [the] plunder."
en.B: "Kings with their armies run, they run away, and the woman who stayed at home shares out the spoil."
en.R: "Kings and their armies run away as fast as they can! The women at home divide up what was taken from them."

decisions.choice: the women's song
decisions.reason: This verse is taken as the news the women of verse 12 spread. It is not certain where their words end; the hard verse 14 is left outside the quotation.

decisions.choice: the beautiful one of the house: the woman at home
decisions.reason: The word (newat) can mean "beautiful one" or "one who dwells". Either way it is the woman who stayed at home and now shares the spoil, as in Judges 5:30.

decisions.choice: flee, they flee: run headlong
decisions.reason: The repeated verb shows the haste of their flight.

decisions.choice: the women
decisions.reason: Readable makes the figure plural, since she stands for all the women at home.

source.text: אִֽם־תִּשְׁכְּבוּן֮ בֵּ֪ין שְׁפַ֫תָּ֥יִם כַּנְפֵ֣י י֭וֹנָה נֶחְפָּ֣ה בַכֶּ֑סֶף וְ֝אֶבְרוֹתֶ֗יהָ בִּֽירַקְרַ֥ק חָרֽוּץ׃

records.literal_gloss: If you lie down between [the] saddlebags, [the] wings of a dove [are] covered with silver and its pinions with greenish gold.

en.L: If you lie down between the sheepfolds — the wings of a dove covered with silver, and its pinions with shimmering gold.
en.B: Even if you men lie among the sheep pens, there are a dove's wings sheathed in silver, its feathers shining with pale gold.
en.R: Even if some of you stayed home by the sheep pens, there is treasure for you: a dove with wings covered in silver and feathers shining with gold.

decisions.choice: the sheepfolds: perhaps the campfires or the saddlebags
decisions.reason: The word (shefattayim) is rare and its meaning is uncertain. A similar word in Judges 5:16 describes the tribe of Reuben, who stayed among the sheepfolds instead of going to battle.

decisions.choice: a hard verse
alternatives: the dove is Israel, enriched by the victory
the dove is a piece of the plunder
decisions.reason: The connection between the two halves is not clear. Most likely those who stayed at home ("you" is plural) still share in the spoil, pictured as a precious dove of silver and gold; or the dove is Israel itself, shining after the victory.

decisions.choice: greenish: with a pale, shimmering color
decisions.reason: The word (yeraqraq) describes a pale greenish or yellowish sheen.

decisions.choice: you men (B); some of you (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" is plural and masculine; Balanced and Readable make that clear.

decisions.choice: there is treasure for you
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the likeliest link between the two halves (m2).

source.text: בְּפָ֘רֵ֤שׂ שַׁדַּ֓י מְלָ֘כִ֤ים בָּ֗הּ תַּשְׁלֵ֥ג בְּצַלְמֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: When [the] Almighty scatters kings in it, it snows on Zalmon.

en.L: When the Almighty scatters kings in it, it snows on Zalmon.
en.B: When the Almighty scattered kings across the land, snow came down on Zalmon.
en.R: When God, the Almighty, scattered the kings in that land, snow fell on Mount Zalmon.

decisions.choice: the Almighty: Shaddai
decisions.reason: Shaddai is an old name for God (Genesis 17:1; Exodus 6:3). Its exact meaning is not certain; the ancient translations took it as "the Almighty".

decisions.choice: it snows on Zalmon: a picture of the scattered enemy
alternatives: the weapons and bodies lay like snow
a snowstorm that routed the enemy
decisions.reason: Zalmon is a hill near Shechem (Judges 9:48); the name sounds like the word for "dark". The picture may be of the fallen or their gear lying white over the dark hill like snow, or of a real snowstorm in the battle. Its sense is no longer clear.

decisions.choice: in it: in the land
decisions.reason: "It" is probably the land of verse 10.

decisions.choice: God,
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the Almighty is God.

source.text: הַר־אֱ֭לֹהִים הַר־בָּשָׁ֑ן הַ֥ר גַּ֝בְנֻנִּ֗ים הַר־בָּשָֽׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: A mountain of God [is the] mountain of Bashan; a mountain of peaks [is the] mountain of Bashan.

en.L: A mountain of God [is the] mountain of Bashan; a mountain of peaks [is the] mountain of Bashan.
en.B: Mount Bashan is a mighty mountain; Mount Bashan is a mountain of many peaks.
en.R: Mount Bashan is a great mountain. It has many high peaks.

decisions.choice: a mountain of God: a mighty mountain
decisions.reason: "Of God" can mean "very great" (36:7, "mountains of God"). The high peaks of Bashan were impressive, but God did not choose them (verse 17).

decisions.choice: Bashan: the high country east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Bashan lay north-east of the Sea of Galilee, a rich land of high mountains, with Mount Hermon at its north end.

source.text: לָ֤מָּה׀תְּֽרַצְּדוּן֮ הָרִ֪ים גַּבְנֻ֫נִּ֥ים הָהָ֗ר חָמַ֣ד אֱלֹהִ֣ים לְשִׁבְתּ֑וֹ אַף־יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִשְׁכֹּ֥ן לָנֶֽצַח׃

records.literal_gloss: Why do you look with envy, mountains of peaks, [at] the mountain God desired for his dwelling? Indeed YHWH will dwell [there] forever.

en.L: Why do you look with envy, mountains of peaks, [at] the mountain God desired for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling? Indeed, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will dwell [there] forever.
en.B: Why do you glare in envy, you many-peaked mountains, at the mountain God longed for as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home? There {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will live for all time.
en.R: You mountains with many peaks, why are you jealous of the mountain God wanted for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will live there forever!

decisions.choice: look with envy: watch jealously
decisions.reason: The verb (ratsad) is found only here; it seems to mean to watch with envy or hostility.

decisions.choice: the mountain God desired: Zion
decisions.reason: The mountain is Zion in Jerusalem, a small hill that God chose over the great peaks (132:13-14; 78:68).

decisions.choice: dwell: live as in a tent
decisions.reason: The verb (shakan) is used of God's dwelling among his people (Exodus 25:8).

source.text: רֶ֤כֶב אֱלֹהִ֗ים רִבֹּתַ֣יִם אַלְפֵ֣י שִׁנְאָ֑ן אֲדֹנָ֥י בָ֝֗ם סִינַ֥י בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] chariots of God [are] twice ten thousand, thousands of repetition; [the] Lord [is] among them; Sinai [is] in holiness.

en.L: The chariots of God [are] twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord [is] among them; Sinai [is] in the holy place.
en.B: God's chariots number twenty thousand, thousands more again; the Lord is among them, and Sinai has come into the holy place.
en.R: God has more chariots than anyone can count, thousands and thousands of them. The Lord is with them. The God of Mount Sinai has come into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy place.

decisions.choice: Sinai is in the holy place
alternatives: the Lord has come from Sinai into the holy place
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "Sinai in holiness": the presence that was on Sinai now fills the sanctuary on Zion. With a small change of letters it would read "the Lord came from Sinai into the holy place", as in Deuteronomy 33:2. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: the chariots of God: his heavenly army
decisions.reason: God comes as a warrior with countless chariots, the army of heaven (2 Kings 6:17; Habakkuk 3:8).

decisions.choice: thousands of repetition: thousands upon thousands
decisions.reason: The word (shin'an) is found only here; it seems to mean repeated thousands, a number beyond counting.

decisions.choice: more chariots than anyone can count
decisions.reason: Readable gives the point of the large numbers.

decisions.choice: the God of Mount Sinai has come
decisions.reason: Readable says what "Sinai in the holy place" means (m1).

source.text: עָ֘לִ֤יתָ לַמָּר֨וֹם׀שָׁ֘בִ֤יתָ שֶּׁ֗בִי לָקַ֣חְתָּ מַ֭תָּנוֹת בָּאָדָ֑ם וְאַ֥ף ס֝וֹרְרִ֗ים לִשְׁכֹּ֤ן׀יָ֬הּ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: You went up to the height; you took captive captives; you took gifts among humankind, and even [the] rebellious, for Yah God to dwell [there].

en.L: You went up to the height; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} took captives captive; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} took gifts among people, and even [among] the rebellious, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} God to dwell [there].
en.B: You climbed to the heights and led away a band of captives; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} accepted tribute from human beings, even from those who rebelled, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} God could make a home there.
en.R: You went up to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} high place, taking prisoners with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You took gifts from people, even from those who fought against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}} God will live there.

decisions.choice: you went up to the height: God's ascent to Zion
decisions.reason: The picture is of a victorious king going up to his capital with his prisoners and the tribute of the defeated. The height is Zion, the mountain of verse 17, and perhaps also heaven above it.

decisions.choice: Ephesians 4:8: "he gave gifts to people"
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse of Christ's ascension: "When he went up on high, he led captivity captive, and he gave gifts to people." The Hebrew says "you took gifts"; an old Aramaic paraphrase and the Syriac translation read "you gave gifts", which Paul's wording agrees with. The conqueror who receives tribute is the one who gives it out to his people (verse 13).

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a shortened form of the name YHWH (as in Exodus 15:2 and in "Hallelu-yah"). It is rendered like the full name, with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: for Yah God to dwell: that God might live there
alternatives: even the rebels must live with the LORD God
decisions.reason: The words can say why God went up (to dwell on Zion), or that even rebels will live under God's rule.

decisions.choice: those who fought against you
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they rebelled against.

source.text: בָּ֤ר֣וּךְ אֲדֹנָי֮ י֤וֹם׀י֥וֹם יַֽעֲמָס־לָ֗נוּ הָ֘אֵ֤ל יְֽשׁוּעָתֵ֬נוּ סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [be the] Lord; day [by] day he carries [a load] for us, the God [who is] our salvation. Selah.

en.L: Blessed [be] the Lord; day by day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} carries [the load] for us, the God of our salvation. Selah
en.B: Blessed be the Lord, who carries our load day after day, the God who saves us. Selah
en.R: Praise the Lord! Every day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} carries our heavy loads. He is the God who saves us. Selah

decisions.choice: carries for us: bears our burden
decisions.reason: The verb ('amas) means to carry a load. With "for us" it most likely means he carries our burden, or carries us (Isaiah 46:3-4).

decisions.choice: the God: 'El
decisions.reason: 'El is a shorter word for God, often used in poetry.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: הָ֤אֵ֣ל׀לָנוּ֮ אֵ֤ל לְֽמוֹשָׁ֫ע֥וֹת וְלֵיהוִ֥ה אֲדֹנָ֑י לַ֝מָּ֗וֶת תּוֹצָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: The God for us [is] a God of saving acts, and to YHWH [the] Lord [belong] the goings out from death.

en.L: The God [who is] for us [is] a God of saving acts, and to {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} the Lord [belong] the ways out from death.
en.B: This God of ours is a God of rescues; the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} holds the ways of escape from death.
en.R: Our God rescues us again and again. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} can bring us out even from death.

decisions.choice: saving acts: many rescues
decisions.reason: The plural (moshaot) means rescue after rescue.

decisions.choice: the goings out from death: escapes from death
alternatives: the ways that lead to death
decisions.reason: The word (totsaot) means the ways out of a place. God holds the exits from death: he can bring his people out when death has closed in.

decisions.choice: GOD the Lord (L); the Lord GOD (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the name comes before "the Lord". As where "the Lord" stands with the name elsewhere, the name is written GOD so that the two are not read as "Lord Lord"; Balanced and Readable use the familiar order.

source.text: אַךְ־אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִמְחַץ֮ רֹ֤אשׁ אֹ֫יְבָ֥יו קָדְקֹ֥ד שֵׂעָ֑ר מִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בַּאֲשָׁמָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Surely God will shatter [the] head of his enemies, [the] crown of hair of [the one] going about in his guilt.

en.L: Surely God will shatter the head of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies, the hairy crown of [one] who goes about in his guilt.
en.B: Yes, God will smash the skulls of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies, the hairy scalps of those who keep walking in their guilt.
en.R: God will surely break the skulls of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies, the long-haired heads of people who keep on sinning.

decisions.choice: the hairy crown: the warrior's long hair
decisions.reason: Warriors let their hair grow long, perhaps under a vow, as a sign of strength (Deuteronomy 32:42; Judges 5:2). Even their pride cannot protect them.

decisions.choice: shatter: strike through
decisions.reason: The verb (machats) is to smash or wound; it returns in verse 24 (110:5-6).

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

source.text: אָמַ֣ר אֲ֭דֹנָי מִבָּשָׁ֣ן אָשִׁ֑יב אָ֝שִׁ֗יב מִֽמְּצֻל֥וֹת יָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] Lord said, From Bashan I will bring back; I will bring back from [the] depths of [the] sea,

en.L: The Lord said, "From Bashan I will bring [them] back; I will bring [them] back from the depths of the sea,
en.B: The Lord has spoken: "I will fetch them back from Bashan, fetch them back from the deepest sea,
en.R: The Lord says, "I will bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} enemies back from Bashan. I will bring them back even from the bottom of the sea.

decisions.choice: bring back: bring the enemies back for judgment
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. In context (verses 22 and 24) it is most likely the enemies: they cannot hide on the highest mountain or in the deepest sea (Amos 9:2-3). Some read it of God bringing his scattered people home.

decisions.choice: a word of God that runs to verse 24
decisions.reason: The Lord's words run to the end of verse 24.

decisions.choice: Bashan and the sea: the heights and the depths
decisions.reason: Bashan's mountains (verse 16) and the depths of the sea are the farthest places a person might flee to.

decisions.choice: them (L, B); my enemies (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no object; every level supplies it (m1).

source.text: לְמַ֤עַן׀תִּֽמְחַ֥ץ רַגְלְךָ֗ בְּ֫דָ֥ם לְשׁ֥וֹן כְּלָבֶ֑יךָ מֵאֹיְבִ֥ים מִנֵּֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: so that your foot may shatter in blood, [the] tongue of your dogs from [the] enemies [has] its portion.

en.L: so that your foot may shatter [them, wading] in blood, [and] the tongue of your dogs [have] its portion from [the] enemies."
en.B: so that you may plunge your feet in blood, and your dogs' tongues may have their share of the enemy."
en.R: Then you will walk through their blood, and your dogs will lick it up."

decisions.choice: may shatter: may strike
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is "shatter", as in verse 22. With one letter different it would read "bathe", as in 58:11 ("he will bathe his feet in the blood of the wicked"), and the ancient Greek translation reads "dip". The Hebrew text is followed; the sense is a complete victory.

decisions.choice: your: Israel's
decisions.reason: God is speaking to his people: "your foot" and "your dogs" are Israel's.

decisions.choice: dogs: a picture of total defeat
decisions.reason: For dogs to lick the blood of the fallen was the worst disgrace (1 Kings 21:19; 22:38). The language is that of ancient war songs.

source.text: רָא֣וּ הֲלִיכוֹתֶ֣יךָ אֱלֹהִ֑ים הֲלִ֘יכ֤וֹת אֵלִ֖י מַלְכִּ֣י בַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: They have seen your processions, God, [the] processions of my God, my King, in the holy [place].

en.L: They have seen {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} processions, God, the processions of my God, my King, in the holy place.
en.B: Your solemn marches have been seen, God, the marches of my God, my King, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} enters the holy place.
en.R: God, people have seen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} marching in a parade to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy place. You are my God and my King.

decisions.choice: processions: the festival march to the temple
decisions.reason: The march of God from Sinai ends in a procession of worshipers going up into the sanctuary, perhaps with the ark (2 Samuel 6:12-15; 24:7-10).

decisions.choice: in the holy place: into the sanctuary, or in holiness
decisions.reason: The word (qodesh) can mean the holy place or holiness itself, as in verse 18.

decisions.choice: my King: God as King
decisions.reason: God is the true King of Israel (5:3; 24:7-10).

decisions.choice: You are my God and my King
decisions.reason: Readable makes the titles a separate sentence.

source.text: קִדְּמ֣וּ שָׁ֭רִים אַחַ֣ר נֹגְנִ֑ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲ֝לָמ֗וֹת תּוֹפֵפֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Singers went in front, musicians behind, in [the] midst of young women playing tambourines.

en.L: Singers went in front, musicians behind, in the midst of young women playing tambourines.
en.B: The singers lead the way, the players of strings follow, and all around them young women beat their tambourines.
en.R: The singers walk in front. The musicians come last. Young women playing tambourines go in the middle.

decisions.choice: musicians: players of stringed instruments
decisions.reason: The word (nogenim) is from the verb for playing strings (see neginot in 67:1).

decisions.choice: young women with tambourines
decisions.reason: Women with hand drums led the songs of victory (Exodus 15:20; Judges 11:34).

source.text: בְּֽ֭מַקְהֵלוֹת בָּרְכ֣וּ אֱלֹהִ֑ים יְ֝הוָ֗ה מִמְּק֥וֹר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: In assemblies bless God, YHWH, from [the] fountain of Israel.

en.L: In [the] assemblies bless God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [you who are] from the fountain of Israel.
en.B: Bless God in the great assemblies; bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you who spring from Israel's fountain.
en.R: Praise God when you gather together! Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you who come from Israel's family line.

decisions.choice: the fountain of Israel: Israel's ancestor
alternatives: the LORD, the fountain of Israel
decisions.reason: A fountain is a source; those "from Israel's fountain" are descendants of Israel, that is, Jacob (Deuteronomy 33:28; Isaiah 48:1). Some take the fountain to be God himself (36:10).

decisions.choice: bless: a call to the worshipers
decisions.reason: This may be the song sung in the procession.

decisions.choice: family line
decisions.reason: Readable says what the fountain stands for (m1).

source.text: שָׁ֤ם בִּנְיָמִ֨ן׀צָעִ֡יר רֹדֵ֗ם שָׂרֵ֣י יְ֭הוּדָה רִגְמָתָ֑ם שָׂרֵ֥י זְ֝בֻל֗וּן שָׂרֵ֥י נַפְתָּלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: There [is] Benjamin, [the] youngest, ruling them, [the] princes of Judah, their throng, [the] princes of Zebulun, [the] princes of Naphtali.

en.L: There [is] Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them, the princes of Judah, their throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
en.B: There goes little Benjamin in the lead, the princes of Judah in their crowded ranks, then Zebulun's princes and Naphtali's princes.
en.R: Little Benjamin, the smallest tribe, leads the way. Next come the leaders of Judah in a great crowd, then the leaders of Zebulun and Naphtali.

decisions.choice: four tribes for all Israel
decisions.reason: Two tribes of the south (Benjamin and Judah) and two of the north (Zebulun and Naphtali) stand for the whole people in the procession. Benjamin was the youngest son of Jacob and the smallest tribe; Israel's first king came from it (1 Samuel 9:21). Zebulun and Naphtali fought bravely in Judges 5:18.

decisions.choice: ruling them: going at their head
decisions.reason: The verb (radah) means to rule; here Benjamin leads the procession.

decisions.choice: their throng: their crowd
decisions.reason: The word (rigmah) is found only here; it seems to mean a dense crowd.

source.text: צִוָּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ עֻ֫זֶּ֥ךָ עוּזָּ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֑ים ז֝֗וּ פָּעַ֥לְתָּ לָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your God has commanded your strength; be strong, God, [you] who have acted for us.

en.L: Your God has commanded your strength; show strength, God, [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] who have acted for us.
en.B: Your God has decreed your strength, Israel. Show {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} might, God, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have acted for us before.
en.R: Israel, your God has decided to make you strong. God, show {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power again, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done for us before.

decisions.choice: your God has commanded: as the Hebrew reads
alternatives: command, God, your strength (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "your God has commanded your strength", spoken to Israel. The ancient Greek translation and some Hebrew manuscripts read "Command, God, your strength", a prayer to God. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: your: Israel's, then God's
decisions.reason: The first half speaks to Israel ("your God ... your strength"); the second turns to God.

decisions.choice: Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one addressed in the first half (m2).

decisions.choice: before
decisions.reason: "You have acted for us" looks back to what God has already done.

source.text: מֵֽ֭הֵיכָלֶךָ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְךָ֤ יוֹבִ֖ילוּ מְלָכִ֣ים שָֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: From your temple at Jerusalem, to you kings will bring a gift.

en.L: From {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple above Jerusalem, kings will bring a gift to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: On account of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple high over Jerusalem, kings will carry tribute to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Kings will come with presents for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} temple stands in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: from your temple: because of your temple
decisions.reason: The "from" can give the reason the kings come, or join the verse to the end of verse 29: show your strength from your temple.

decisions.choice: kings bring gifts: tribute to the great King
decisions.reason: Defeated or allied kings sent tribute to the king they served (72:10; 1 Kings 10:23-25). Here the nations pay homage to God at his temple.

decisions.choice: at Jerusalem: over Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "over" or "above": the temple stands high above the city.

source.text: גְּעַ֨ר חַיַּ֪ת קָנֶ֡ה עֲדַ֤ת אַבִּירִ֨ים׀בְּעֶגְלֵ֬י עַמִּ֗ים מִתְרַפֵּ֥ס בְּרַצֵּי־כָ֑סֶף בִּזַּ֥ר עַ֝מִּ֗ים קְרָב֥וֹת יֶחְפָּֽצוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Rebuke [the] beast of [the] reed, [the] herd of bulls with [the] calves of [the] peoples, trampling himself with pieces of silver; he has scattered peoples [who] delight in wars.

en.L: Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, [each] humbling himself with pieces of silver; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has scattered peoples [who] delight in wars.
en.B: Rebuke the beast that lurks among the reeds, that herd of bulls with the calves of the nations, until they come bowing low with bars of silver. God has scattered the peoples who love war.
en.R: Speak sternly to the beast that hides in the reeds by the river and to the herd of bulls with their calves, the proud nations and their people. Make them bow down and bring silver. God has scattered nations that love war.

decisions.choice: the beast of the reeds: Egypt
decisions.reason: The animal of the reeds is probably the crocodile or hippopotamus of the Nile, a picture of Egypt (Ezekiel 29:3); verse 32 names Egypt. The bulls are the strong rulers, the calves the nations under them.

decisions.choice: trampling himself with pieces of silver: bowing low with tribute
alternatives: trampling on those who lust for silver
decisions.reason: The words are very hard. The verb seems to mean to stamp or to throw oneself down; with "pieces of silver" it probably pictures the nations humbling themselves and bringing silver as tribute. Its sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: he has scattered: as the Hebrew reads
alternatives: scatter (a prayer, as in the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he has scattered"; the ancient translations read the same letters as a prayer, "scatter".

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one who scatters.

decisions.choice: by the river ... the proud nations and their people
decisions.reason: Readable explains the animal pictures (m1).

source.text: יֶאֱתָ֣יוּ חַ֭שְׁמַנִּים מִנִּ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם כּ֥וּשׁ תָּרִ֥יץ יָ֝דָ֗יו לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Envoys will come from Egypt; Cush will make her hands run to God.

en.L: Envoys will come from Egypt; Cush will make her hands run to God.
en.B: High officials will come out of Egypt; Cush will quickly lift its hands in prayer to God.
en.R: Leaders will come from Egypt. The people of Cush will hurry to raise their hands to God.

decisions.choice: envoys: high officials
decisions.reason: The word (chashmannim) is found only here; it probably means nobles or envoys. Some connect it with bronze or a red dye, gifts brought from Egypt.

decisions.choice: Cush: the land south of Egypt
decisions.reason: Cush lay along the Nile south of Egypt, in what is now Sudan; for Israel it was the far edge of the world.

decisions.choice: make her hands run: hurry to stretch out her hands
decisions.reason: Stretching out the hands is a gesture of prayer and of submission (Exodus 9:29; Isaiah 1:15).

decisions.choice: in prayer (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the raised hands mean (m3).

source.text: מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָ֭אָרֶץ שִׁ֣ירוּ לֵאלֹהִ֑ים זַמְּר֖וּ אֲדֹנָ֣י סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praise [to the] Lord. Selah.

en.L: Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praise [to] the Lord. Selah
en.B: Sing to God, all you kingdoms on earth; make music for the Lord. Selah
en.R: All you nations of the world, sing to God! Sing praise to the Lord! Selah

decisions.choice: the call goes out to all kingdoms
decisions.reason: After Egypt and Cush, every kingdom is called to praise Israel's God.

decisions.choice: a call that runs into verse 34
decisions.reason: Verse 34 says who the Lord is ("to the one who rides ..."). Because of the Selah, each level ends this verse and begins verse 34 with its own call.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: לָ֭רֹכֵב בִּשְׁמֵ֣י שְׁמֵי־קֶ֑דֶם הֵ֥ן יִתֵּ֥ן בְּ֝קוֹלוֹ ק֣וֹל עֹֽז׃

records.literal_gloss: To the one who rides in [the] heavens of [the] heavens of old; see, he gives with his voice a voice of strength.

en.L: [Sing] to the one who rides in the heavens of heavens of old; see, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, a voice of strength.
en.B: Sing to the one who rides across the ancient heavens, the heaven of heavens; listen, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lets {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice ring out, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice of power.
en.R: Sing to the one who rides through the oldest, highest skies. Listen! He thunders with a powerful voice.

decisions.choice: the heavens of heavens: the highest heavens
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 10:14, the phrase means the very highest heaven. "Of old" says they have been there since the beginning.

decisions.choice: his voice: thunder
decisions.reason: God's voice is heard in the thunder (29:3-9; 18:14).

decisions.choice: Sing
decisions.reason: The verse continues the call of verse 33; each level repeats "sing" after the Selah.

decisions.choice: thunders
decisions.reason: Readable names what God's voice is here (m2).

source.text: תְּנ֥וּ עֹ֗ז לֵֽאלֹ֫הִ֥ים עַֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל גַּאֲוָת֑וֹ וְ֝עֻזּ֗וֹ בַּשְּׁחָקִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Give strength to God; over Israel [is] his majesty and his strength [is] in the clouds.

en.L: Give strength to God; over Israel [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} majesty, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength [is] in the clouds.
en.B: Declare that power belongs to God! His majesty rests over Israel; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} might is in the clouds.
en.R: Tell everyone how strong God is! His greatness is over Israel. His power fills the skies.

decisions.choice: give strength to God: acknowledge his power
decisions.reason: To "give" strength to God is to declare that it is his (29:1).

decisions.choice: majesty: his lofty greatness
decisions.reason: The word (ga'avah) is height or majesty, used of God's exalted rule.

decisions.choice: declare (B); tell everyone (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what giving strength means (m1).

source.text: נ֤וֹרָ֥א אֱלֹהִ֗ים מִֽמִּקְדָּ֫שֶׁ֥יךָ אֵ֤ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל ה֤וּא נֹתֵ֨ן׀עֹ֖ז וְתַעֲצֻמ֥וֹת לָעָ֗ם בָּר֥וּךְ אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Awesome [is] God from your sanctuaries; [the] God of Israel, he [is] giving strength and might to the people. Blessed [be] God!

en.L: Awesome [are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}], God, from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sanctuaries; the God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is the one] giving strength and might to the people. Blessed [be] God!
en.B: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} inspire awe from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy places; Israel's God is the one who gives {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people strength and might. Blessed be God!
en.R: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are wonderful and fearsome as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy place. The God of Israel makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people strong and powerful. Praise God!

decisions.choice: from your sanctuaries: God addressed again
decisions.reason: "Your" turns to speak to God for a moment. The plural "sanctuaries" may mean the holy place with its courts, or God's dwelling in heaven and on Zion.

decisions.choice: might: great strength
decisions.reason: The word (ta'atsumot) is found only here; it is from a root meaning "to be strong".

decisions.choice: the psalm ends in blessing
decisions.reason: The psalm that began with God rising against his enemies ends with God giving strength to his people.

decisions.choice: you are (L); you inspire (B, R)
decisions.reason: Because "your sanctuaries" speaks to God, each level makes the first line address him.
